newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia outlines Zastava car plant 97 target.
newsitem.headline: Serbia outlines Zastava car plant 97 target.

text.p: The Serbian government presented production plans on Tuesday for its Zastava car producer as a part of its wider strategy to kick-start the country's idle metal-processing industry.
Serbia's first Privatisation Minister Milan Beko said the state must also help companies like Zastava revive their production along with creating the right business climate.
"The important thing is to help enterprises revive their production," Beko told a news conference.
Zastava has proposed a programme worth 970 million dinars ($170.7 million) to initiate production of 22,250 cars from April to the end of the year.
Some 12,250 cars were earmarked for sales at home and 10,000 cars for exports to Macedonia, Egypt, Jordan and Ecuador to the value of some 64 million German marks.
The programme is also expected to bring 193 million dinars into empty state coffers.
"The programme is good and possible to carry out. The state must provide financial aid," Beko said.
The government promised to secure 70.2 million dinars in initial funding to kick-start the production, mainly through commercial bank loans.
"Jugobanka will help by discounting letters of credit issued by foreign companies for Zastava exports and Beobanka will provide initial dinar funds to be used locally," Beko said.
Succesful revival of Zastava car production means rehabilitation and recovery of its subcontractors, especially of the Belgrade industries.
"But besides the effect on production it has a social impact too," he said.
Zastava's programme would revive production in some 200 firms in 63 towns throughout the country.
In the first three months of the year Zastava produced some 2,000 cars only because of the lack of working capital.

In 1996, despite the government help Zastava failed to produce targeted 15,000 cars. The output was up 30 percent on the previous year to about 10,000 cars, but still a far cry from the pre-war annual output of 200,000 cars.

Srboljub Vasovic, executive director of the entire Zastava Group, saw the targeted output as extremely high for the car plant at present but said it was a minimum it had to produce to keep production going.

"This programme is to be or not to be for Zastava. It is an enormous obligation for all of us, but it simply must be carried out as it secures production continuity not only for the car plant but for the entire group and regular payments for employees," Vasovic said.
"It would also secure necessary working capital for the beginning of the next year."
